pacioli.name: Pacioli, Fra Luca
pacioli.role: Franciscan Mathematician of Borgo Sansepolcro; Author of the Summa (1494) and De Divina Proportione (1509)
pacioli.bio: Born at Borgo Sansepolcro, educated in the workshop of Piero della Francesca and hosted in Rome by Leon Battista Alberti; lectured on Euclid and practical mathematics across Perugia, Zara, Naples, Rome, Milan (alongside Leonardo da Vinci), Florence, Pisa, Bologna, and Venice, seeing his encyclopedic Summa through Paganino de' Paganini's press in November 1494.
works: Summa de arithmetica, geometria, proportioni et proportionalita (Venice, 1494)

guidobaldo-da-montefeltro.name: Montefeltro, Guidobaldo da
guidobaldo-da-montefeltro.role: Duke of Urbino; Dedicatee of Pacioli's Summa (1494)
guidobaldo-da-montefeltro.bio: Son of Federico da Montefeltro and Battista Sforza; humanist prince of Urbino to whom Pacioli dedicated both the Italian and Latin dedicatory epistles of the 1494 Summa and fashioned wooden models of the regular and dependent polyhedra.

federico-da-montefeltro.name: Montefeltro, Federico da
federico-da-montefeltro.role: Duke of Urbino, Condottiero, and Builder of the Palazzo Ducale
federico-da-montefeltro.bio: Father of Guidobaldo da Montefeltro; patron of Piero della Francesca, Francesco di Giorgio Martini, and Luciano Laurana, celebrated by Pacioli on prelim. fol. 2v for the architectural proportion of the Ducal Palace of Urbino.

marco-sanudo.name: Sanudo, Marco
marco-sanudo.role: Venetian Patrician, Mathematician, and Financial Patron of the 1494 Summa
marco-sanudo.bio: Learned Venetian nobleman praised by Pacioli on prelim. fol. 1v as 'astrologiae, geometriae, arithmeticaeque cultor exquisitissimus', whose financial patronage underwrote the printing of the 1494 Summa in Venice.

paganino-de-paganini.name: Paganini, Paganino de'
paganino-de-paganini.role: Master Printer from Brescia in Venice
paganino-de-paganini.bio: Master typographer from Brescia operating in Venice who cut the marginal mathematical woodblocks and printed both Pacioli's Summa (Nov. 10–20, 1494) and De Divina Proportione plus Euclidis Opera (1509).

agostino-barbarigo.name: Barbarigo, Agostino
agostino-barbarigo.role: Doge of the Republic of Venice (1486 – 1501)
agostino-barbarigo.bio: Doge of Venice under whose signory Paganino de' Paganini and Fra Luca Pacioli were granted a ten-year printing privilege recorded in the colophon of Part II, fol. 76r.

pompilio.name: Pompilio, Paolo
pompilio.bio: Author of the Latin elegiac epigram in praise of Fra Luca Pacioli printed on prelim. fol. 1v of the 1494 Summa.
works: Epigramma ad Lucam Paciolum (Summa, prelim. fol. 1v)

giorgio-sommaripa.name: Sommaripa, Giorgio
giorgio-sommaripa.bio: Author of the Italian caudate sonnet celebrating Pacioli's universal synthesis of arithmetic, geometry, and Venetian double-entry ledger craft on prelim. fol. 1v.
works: Sonetto a Fra Luca Pacioli (Summa, prelim. fol. 1v)

piero-della-francesca.name: Francesca, Piero della
piero-della-francesca.role: Master Painter and Mathematician of Borgo Sansepolcro
piero-della-francesca.bio: Fellow townsman and mathematical mentor of Pacioli; praised on fol. 68v as 'el monarca a li tempi nostri de la pictura' and author of the Trattato d'abaco, De prospectiva pingendi, and Libellus de quinque corporibus regularibus.

alberti.name: Alberti, Leon Battista
alberti.bio: Hosted young Pacioli in Rome; cited on fol. 68v alongside Vitruvius and Piero della Francesca on architectural and pictorial symmetry.

leonardo-pisano.name: Leonardo Pisano (Fibonacci)
leonardo-pisano.role: Pisan Mathematician; Principal Medieval Source of the Summa
leonardo-pisano.bio: Explicitly acknowledged by Pacioli on Part I, fol. 1v as his foremost authority: wherever no other author is named in the Summa, the reader is to understand the doctrine derives from Leonardo Pisano's Liber Abaci (1202/1228) and Practica Geometriae (1220).

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.role: Greek Geometer; Author of the Elements
euclid.bio: Revered throughout the Summa as the supreme deductive authority across arithmetic (Books VII–IX), proportion (Book V), irrational binomials and apotomes (Book X), plane geometry (Books I–VI), and the regular solids (Books XI–XIII).

boethius.name: Boethius, Anicius Manlius Severinus
boethius.role: Roman Philosopher and Codifier of the Quadrivium
boethius.bio: Transmitted Nicomachus's arithmetic and musical ratio nomenclature (multiplex, superparticularis, superpartiens) into the Latin scholastic curriculum expounded in Summa Part I, Dist. I & VI.

jordanus-nemorarius.name: Jordanus de Nemore (Jordanus Nemorarius)
jordanus-nemorarius.bio: Cited by Pacioli on Part I, fol. 1v and throughout Distinctio VI for speculative arithmetic and proportion theory (De elementis arismetice artis, De numeris datis).

campanus.name: Campanus of Novara
campanus.role: Medieval Commentator and Editor of the Latin Euclid
campanus.bio: Papal chaplain whose Latin edition and scholia on Euclid's Elements (printed at Venice by Erhard Ratdolt in 1482 and revised by Pacioli in 1509) supplied Pacioli's proposition numbering and proportion commentary.

archimedes.name: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes.bio: Cited in Summa Part II, Dist. III (fol. 31r) for the 96-gon bounds 3 10/71 < pi < 3 1/7, Dist. V for sphere-and-cylinder mensuration, and Dist. VIII (fol. 70r, prob. 20) for hydrostatic volume measurement by displaced fluid.

heron.name: Heron of Alexandria
heron.bio: Discoverer of the semiperimeter area formula sqrt(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)) transmitted via Arabic intermediaries and Leonardo Pisano into Summa Part II, Dist. I, Cap. 8 (fol. 9v).

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy, Claudius
ptolemy.bio: Cited in Summa Part II, Dist. III for chord tables and cyclic quadrilaterals from Book I of the Almagest.

vitruvius.name: Vitruvius Pollio, Marcus
vitruvius.bio: Cited on Summa Part I, fol. 68v on architectural proportion and human symmetry.

sacrobosco.name: Sacrobosco, Johannes de (John of Hollywood)
sacrobosco.role: Scholastic Astronomer and Algorist at Paris
sacrobosco.bio: Acknowledged on Part I, fol. 1v as a standard authority on Hindu-Arabic algorism and spherical astronomy.

al-khwarizmi.name: al-Khwārizmī, Muḥammad ibn Mūsā
al-khwarizmi.role: Founder of Hisāb al-jabr wa'l-muqābala in Baghdad
al-khwarizmi.bio: Established the six canonical positive-coefficient linear and quadratic equations and their geometric gnomon demonstrations inherited by Leonardo Pisano and expounded in Summa Part I, Dist. VIII (fols. 145r–146r).
works: Al-Kitāb al-mukhtaṣar fī ḥisāb al-jabr wa'l-muqābala

prosdocimo-de-beldomandi.name: Beldomandi, Prosdocimo de'
prosdocimo-de-beldomandi.role: Paduan Mathematician, Astronomer, and Music Theorist
prosdocimo-de-beldomandi.bio: Cited by Pacioli on Part I, fol. 1v among his foremost Italian predecessors in algorism and musical proportion.

biagio-pelacani.name: Pelacani da Parma, Biagio (Blasius of Parma)
biagio-pelacani.role: Scholastic Natural Philosopher and Theorist of Proportions
biagio-pelacani.bio: Cited on Part I, fol. 1v and in Distinctio VI on kinematic and geometric proportions.

pascal.name: Pascal, Blaise
pascal.role: French Geometer and Co-Founder of Mathematical Probability
pascal.bio: In his July–October 1654 correspondence with Pierre de Fermat, resolved the interrupted-game Problem of Points first printed in Pacioli's 1494 Summa (fol. 197r–197v) via backward expectation and the arithmetic triangle.

fermat.name: Fermat, Pierre de
fermat.role: French Mathematician and Co-Founder of Probability and Number Theory
fermat.bio: Resolved both two-player and multi-player cases of Pacioli's Problem of Points in 1654 via equiprobable completion sequences and discovered Fermat's Little Theorem governing Mersenne primes (cf. Summa fol. 8r).

scipione-del-ferro.name: Ferro, Scipione del
scipione-del-ferro.role: Bolognese Mathematician; Discoverer of the Depressed Cubic Formula
scipione-del-ferro.bio: Colleague of Pacioli at the University of Bologna (1501–1502) who, inspired directly by Pacioli's 1494 challenge on fol. 150r, discovered the radical solution to x^3 + px = q around 1515.

tartaglia.name: Tartaglia, Niccolò Fontana
tartaglia.role: Venetian Mathematician and Translator of Euclid and Archimedes
tartaglia.bio: Rediscovered the cubic solution in Venice (1535), criticized Pacioli's Problem of Points rule in his General Trattato (1556), and published the first Italian translation of Euclid (1543).
works: General Trattato di numeri et misure (1556)

cardano.name: Cardano, Gerolamo
cardano.role: Milanese Physician and Algebraist; Author of the Ars Magna (1545)
cardano.bio: Opened Chapter I of his Ars Magna (1545) by recalling Fra Luca Pacioli's 1494 declaration that cubics were as impossible as squaring the circle before publishing the general cubic and quartic solutions of del Ferro, Tartaglia, and Ferrari.
works: Artis Magnae, sive de Regulis Algebraicis (1545)
